title: Ser — who and what
vocabFocus: Ser: soy, eres, es, somos, son
practiceFocus: Say who you are, then who someone else is

points.title: Five forms, no article before a job
points.rule: Day 1 was soy and me llamo. Hoy es from day 2 is the same es. Ser is for who someone is, where they are from, and a lasting quality. Say soy, eres, es, somos, son. Do not put un or una before a job. Put no before the verb to negate. Use -o for a man and -a for a woman on these jobs: ingeniero, ingeniera, profesor, profesora.

grammar.notYet: Vosotros (sois) and estar. You will hear sois in Spain; you do not need to say it. Gender beyond these job endings waits until a later phrase needs it.

phrases.note: No un or una before a job. This is the same fact as trabajo como ingeniero from day 1.
Profesora for a woman, profesor for a man. Ingeniera and ingeniero work the same way.

phrases.spanish: Hoy es lunes y ella es Ana.
phrases.english: Today is Monday and she is Ana.
phrases.note: Es is the same word for the day and for a person.

lines.speaker: Pablo
lines.english: Hi! My name is Pablo. What is your name?

lines.speaker: Sofía
lines.english: My name is Sofía. Are you from here?

lines.speaker: Pablo
lines.english: Yes, I am from here. And you?

lines.speaker: Sofía
lines.spanish: No, soy de Valencia. Soy profesora.
lines.english: No, I am from Valencia. I am a teacher.

lines.speaker: Pablo
lines.english: I am an engineer. Who is he?

lines.speaker: Sofía
lines.english: He is my friend. We are friends.

practice.title: Who you are
practice.instruction: Introduce yourself again: name, origin, and job with soy. Then say who one other person is, using es. Aim for ten short sentences.
tips: Ser is for identity, origin, and lasting qualities.
No un or una before a job. Hoy es and ella es are the same es.
